and during this famine fewer than a hundred souls were found in it.
And in the year 463 [of the Arabs],
[the Sultan went against] {OCR?} Arkestia, which is the city of Arjish, and conquered it,
and made a great slaughter in it,
and took captives and sent [them] to Khorasan.
And he likewise did also in the city of Manzikert.
And he went to Mayperqat, which was held by the Arabs,
and took from its lord more than a hundred thousand dinars {OCR?},
and passed by Amid.
And he approached its wall,
and passed his hand over it and over his face,
as if to be blessed by its strength.
And he went to Sibabarak (to Sababarak?), which was held by the Romans,
and took from them [many] thousands of {OCR?} dinars,
and left them.
And from there he went and encamped against Edessa,
and attacked it for many days,
and was not able to conquer it,
but they cut down its trees
and destroyed its gardens.
And the Edessenes agreed to give him fifty {OCR?} thousand dinars,
and that he should depart from them.
And when the Sultan consented,
the Edessenes said:
"We cannot give anything until you burn the siege engines (tortoises),"
"and the mangonels,"
"and all the weapons of war;"
"for we fear lest you deceive us,"
"and take the gold,"
"and not stop the war."
And when the Sultan trusted them and burned the weapons of war,
the Edessenes showed contempt and gave nothing.
And the Sultan left them,
and in bitter grief crossed the Euphrates.
And an envoy of Diogenes, king of the Romans, reached him and said to the Sultan:
"If on account of Mabbugh you were moved from your territory and came,"
"behold, we will restore Mabbugh to you again,"
"and you, restore to us Arjish and Manzikert,"
"and we will give you every year the customary tribute."
And when the Sultan accepted and returned as far as the city of Khilat,
Afshin sent and informed him:
"Behold, I entered the territory of the Romans and came out with great plunder,"
"and there is no one among the Romans who confronted us."
And the Sultan took courage,
and with swift steps turned back again to the territory of the Romans in great joy,
so that many of the camels {OCR?} carrying his baggage perished on the way from the frantic march.
